## Context 

- Special issue: methods in the history of economic thought (HET).

- Aim: contribute a methodological essay showing how quantitative tools can enrich HET.

- A concrete case study, not a review of methods.

## Our contribution

- The meanings of rationality in economics in the 20<sup>th</sup> century: 
  - Interests for many historians.  
  - Focus on how computational methods help to draw large picture. 

. . . 

- A concrete methodological discussion following the workflow of our analysis: 
  - What is challenging, what worked well, what did not, what could be improved.

## Sentence embeddings

. . . 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false 
#| warning: false
#| label: tbl-top_sentences
#| tbl-cap: "Closest sentences from our corpus to the fake sentence 'Economic agents are supposed to be rational.'"


# load data OUTPUT_FILE = top_5_sentences_to_fake_sentence.feather

data <- arrow::read_feather(here::here(data_path, "top_5_sentences_to_fake_sentence.feather"))

data |> 
  filter(rank < 4, year %in% c(2000)) |>
  # kable the table
  select(year, sentence, similarity) |>
  knitr::kable() |> 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = F)
```
